title: Knowledge check: Composable Lifecycle and Side Effects

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Composable Lifecycle and Side Effects”?
options: Leave stale asynchronous work running and let it overwrite newer results.
Expect watch() to run immediately by default for every source.
Use watch() for explicit sources or watchEffect() for automatically tracked dependencies when a side effect is required; clean up asynchronous work.
Use computed() for every side effect.
questions.answer_key: Use watch() for explicit sources or watchEffect() for automatically tracked dependencies when a side effect is required; clean up asynchronous work.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Composable Lifecycle and Side Effects directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Lifecycle hooks inside composables”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Assume nextTick() runs before Vue’s queued DOM update.
Use lifecycle hooks when the component reaches the required phase, and remove timers, listeners, and subscriptions during cleanup.
Read a DOM element before it has mounted.
Register a global listener on every update without cleanup.
questions.answer_key: Use lifecycle hooks when the component reaches the required phase, and remove timers, listeners, and subscriptions during cleanup.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Lifecycle hooks inside composables”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Composable Lifecycle and Side Effects” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
